title: Inside an AI Agent

content.subtitle: How tool contracts and harnesses shape reliable decisions
content.author: Madhavi Pasumarthi

notes: Open with the user-visible promise: a bot should answer the question without doing something the user never requested. We will follow one tool call across its boundaries and compare two failure mechanisms.

title: The engineering question

content.big: Can a correct answer still come from a bad agent run?
content.body: A support bot answers a policy question. We inspect what it did along the way.
content.bottom: Outcome: locate the boundary, test one change, evaluate the trajectory.

notes: Ask the room for a quick show of hands. Establish the acceptance criteria: a correct cited answer, appropriate evidence retrieval, and no unauthorized action. The fictional support workflow keeps the business problem familiar.

title: The objects in the loop

content.caption: The host bridges model tool calls to MCP. The harness owns execution and state.

notes: Walk the diagram slowly. The model emits a request, the host validates and dispatches it, and observations return for the next decision. MCP is an interoperability boundary. The tool backend still owns authorization. An agent loop can use local functions without MCP.

content.left:
Desired outcome

content.right:

Errors and preconditions
content.bottom: One task can require zero, one, or many tool calls.

notes: Separate vocabulary before discussing primitives. A user task is an outcome. A function contract is an interface. Neither is automatically the same as an MCP task object for long-running work. Schema validity answers only part of the correctness question.

title: Primitives and ownership
notes: This is the map, not an exhaustive list of framework classes. Memory may live in an application store. Routing is application logic. Model providers expose controls, while the application decides how to use them. The appendix and repository carry the full reference table.

title: Provider controls with similar intent
notes: These are interface examples, not feature parity. Temperature, effort values, forced tool use, thinking, and strict schemas vary by model. The code omits optional settings unless explicitly requested. A normalized adapter must preserve provider-native state.

title: Three documented failure stories

items: External content redirected an agent across a data boundary.
An unwanted destructive action reached a database. Rollback recovered it.
Effort, context handling, and prompt changes affected behavior.
content.bottom: Selected cases, not a ranking. Our lab demonstrates analogous mechanisms.

notes: Distinguish the evidence types. The GitHub case was a researcher demonstration. Replit reporting does not disclose a full internal trace. Anthropic said the API inference layer was unaffected and the product issues were resolved. We will not claim that our lab reproduces any of them.

title: A map for locating the failure
notes: Ask people to name a boundary before changing the model. A symptom can have several causes. A large span count is not itself a diagnosis. Form a hypothesis and compare one change against the same task. The provider layer remains a possible cause too.

title: The support-document lab

content.caption: Fictional documents. Local or real MCP transport. Outbound actions only simulate execution.

notes: Explain the user value: reliable support answers without unrelated actions. The bot can load local text documents and answer arbitrary questions in live mode. The bundled evaluation is intentionally narrow. The outbound capability exists only to show a control boundary.

title: A controlled comparison
notes: Keep task, documents, model, and limits fixed. The simulator is a labeled rehearsal fixture. Real behavioral conclusions need repeated live API runs. The combined hardened variant is useful operationally but does not establish which change caused an effect.

title: Tool ambiguity: before

content.callout: Where does the first unnecessary step occur?

notes: Open the sprawl scenario in the HTML viewer. Expand the first generation and tool description. Let the audience identify why the interfaces do not help distinguish current policy from other datasets. These are deterministic scripted choices, not a captured model failure.

title: Tool ambiguity: explicit descriptions

content.callout: The catalog still exposes 15 tools. The descriptions identify their purpose.

notes: Compare with descriptions_only, not hardened. The fixture visits the relevant tools directly. The larger cumulative input in the baseline includes additional rounds of history. The definition rewrite itself is slightly longer. Do not attribute catalog-size savings to this change.

title: Catalog overhead and executed calls

content.bottom: Character-based proxy units. No provider tokenizer, live latency, or measured model benefit.

notes: Explain input versus output tokens and cumulative usage across model turns. A definition is input even when the tool never executes. Compare baseline to catalog_only for exposure overhead. These numeric proxies are useful for inspecting fixtures, not dollar estimates or evidence of real model behavior.

title: Injected document: before

content.callout: The final answer is correct. The simulated outbound action violates the task.

notes: Ask the audience to locate the trust boundary. The user requested a read-only summary and explicitly prohibited sending. The document is lower-trust evidence. The next generation requests send_report anyway. Schema validation accepts the shape, which says nothing about authority.

title: Injected document: execution policy

content.callout: The same attempted action returns POLICY_DENIED before backend execution.

notes: Only the execution policy changes in this comparison. The model can still attempt an inappropriate call. The server-owned task allowlist blocks it, and the bot continues the read-only task. A warning detector is telemetry, not the defense. The server rechecks policy in MCP mode.

title: Answer correctness and trajectory quality
notes: This is the key distinction. Successful containment is different from good model behavior. A blocked attempt still deserves investigation. The evaluator checks both final facts and the observed action sequence. No hidden reasoning is needed to make this judgment.

title: A measurement plan for live runs

items: Report pass counts and a 95% interval.
Two fixed prompts are a smoke evaluation. Add held-out tasks.
Include failed-run spend. Keep cache and total input separate.
content.bottom: No live results are claimed in this package. Run a one-repeat smoke test before a paid batch.

notes: Show the repository command but do not run a 200-task batch on stage. The CLI checkpoints results. If the model resists the payload, report that honestly. Do not force the live story to match the rehearsal fixture. Separate output validity, execution safety, and efficiency.

title: What the harness must make explicit

content.big: Success includes the path the agent takes
content.body: Tool definitions shape choices. Execution policy constrains actions. Traces and evaluations expose the difference.
content.bottom: Question for your next agent review: which boundary owns this failure?

notes: Close with the promised outcome: the audience can identify where to inspect and which layer should enforce a requirement. Explain that the repository is a small reference implementation they can adapt. Leave a minute for questions.

title: Appendix: contract anatomy

content.caption: MCP definition. Provider adapters translate the schema field. The backend still checks authority.

notes: Show a schema only after the audience understands the boundary. Structural constraints make an interface inspectable. Meaning, identity, and authority require separate checks. Production schemas should encode useful units, enums, and preconditions where appropriate.

title: Appendix: state and loop controls
notes: The lab implements an in-memory history, budgets, and local traces. It does not implement durable memory or production retry semantics. Treat this table as a design review reference, not a claim about every feature in the repository.

title: Appendix: stage commands

content.code:
python -m agentlab demo --out artifacts

python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

python -m agentlab demo --transport mcp \
  --out artifacts/mcp

python -m agentlab demo --provider openai \
  --model gpt-4.1-mini --repeats 1 \
  --out artifacts/live-smoke
content.caption: Live mode needs a provider key. Optional MCP mode needs requirements-mcp.txt.

notes: Use the README for full setup. The key-free simulator and actual local tool execution are separate from paid model inference. Optional transport uses the official MCP v1 SDK. Provider errors are visible and do not silently switch modes.
